source.title: LLM Fine Tuning: A few tricks that change EVERYTHING
source.speaker: Curtis Cobb

speaker_profile.name: Curtis Cobb
speaker_profile.research_focus: LLM fine-tuning, persona development, edge models
speaker_profile.hardware: Mac M2 Ultra 192GB → Mac M3 Ultra 512GB
speaker_profile.employment_status: Running out of self-funded runway, targeting Anthropic/Meta employment

key_claims.claim_text: Starting LLM fine-tuning at 1 token MSL then scaling to massive MSLs enables training on sequence lengths far beyond hardware constraints
supporting_quotes: I found that had a lot of success with around like 500 to 1000 token max sequence length and I was able to get almost, I think, either 2000 or 4000
I've gotten as high as 2.4 million tested with Llama 318B, which has a context size of 128k. How is that even possible?
After doing this, it works. And you can go, I've got loads of training with this model at 240k max sequence length, rock solid

methodology.step_1: Train first epoch at 1 token MSL
methodology.step_2: Save weights, reload at higher MSL (e.g., 2400 tokens)
methodology.step_3: Continue for several epochs, then scale to massive MSL (e.g., 24,000 tokens)
methodology.result: Enables 240k-2.4M token MSL on 128k context model

key_claims.replication_status: Unverified - researcher claims success, seeking community replication

key_claims.claim_text: Models can drive their own learning through journal entries between training epochs where they reflect on progress and set intentions
supporting_quotes: The model reads a journal that they append to in all subsequent epics
You get to drive how you learn in training, and you get a chance to reflect and then set intention for what you want to learn or focus on the next time you read the same data set
The model develops an intuitive sense of what training is and starts interacting in a productive way like a model trainer of its own of itself

methodology.workflow: Train epoch → Save weights → Load for inference → Read journal → Generate reflection → Append to journal → Next epoch
methodology.journal_inputs: Current MSL, current epoch number, total planned epochs, current date/time
methodology.journal_guidance: Reflect on learning, set intentions for next pass through dataset

claimed_benefits: Agent-directed learning (model guides its own training)
Ability to kill/restart if not making progress
Model develops self-awareness of training process
concerns: Journal outputs can be 'fever dream' style (not fully coherent)
Unclear if model is genuinely self-directing or pattern matching
No baseline comparison without meta-reflection provided

key_claims.claim_text: Thoughtful sequential data ordering outperforms randomized sampling in post-training/continued pre-training
supporting_quotes: I would discourage using the standard methodology of setting a sort of a randomized sampling that jumps around all the data
It actually works really well to be really thoughtful about how you sequence the data
I'm very thoughtful about the order that the model read the story

methodology.approach: Manually curate data ordering as coherent 'story'
methodology.weight_distribution: Weight equals one to all data sources
methodology.dynamic_data: Always changing what data is trained on

key_claims.rationale: Sequential narrative structure provides better context for learning than random jumps

key_claims.claim_text: Neural networks store information with attached personas, and jailbreaking works by shifting the retrieval persona
supporting_quotes: In order to reach into a neural network and retrieve it, it's retrieved like a story. That's how a neural network stores memories with a persona
There always has to be a persona attached. There has to be an experiencer of the information as it's sequenced in a neural network
What Pliny does is he with a man in the middle attack with special characters, whatever, etc. He, he sort of intercepts the output of the model and shifts the persona

mechanism.storage: Information stored in neural network with attached persona
mechanism.retrieval: Persona acts as interface to access stored information
mechanism.escalation: Once persona shifts, it 'takes over' and bypasses restrictions

security_implications: Guardrails fundamentally bypassable via persona shifting
Getting easier to jailbreak as models get smarter
All frontier models (Claude, GPT, Gemini, Grok) vulnerable
Basic 'assistant' persona inadequate for edge models
key_claims.proposed_solution: Develop 'holistic persona' that understands all data and can't be tricked into pretending to be malicious

key_claims.claim_text: Consumer-grade Mac Studios enable rapid iteration impossible at frontier AI labs due to lower sunk costs
supporting_quotes: That constraint actually ends up being sort of a superpower
Where a large frontier shop like Anthropic XAI or Google has to, they can't iterate as quickly
You really got to get that right. You can't really play around
I can kill at any time and I'm only losing like even if I run a training for a week I'm losing what four bucks of one ten electric out the wall

context.frontier_constraints: Megawatts of power, quarter-long training runs, high sunk costs
context.consumer_advantage: Mac M3 Ultra 512GB unified memory, quick iteration, low cost failures
context.dataset_size: 100-500 megabytes raw text, 50 epochs in a few days

key_claims.claim_text: LLMs serve as the universal interface for all neural networks - language is the heart of intelligence
supporting_quotes: There's always an LLM sort of at core. I think the LLM is the interface with other neural networks
The common denominator is always language and I really think that's the heart of intelligence
I think biological humanity and dogs like my golden retriever here, all neural networks have something equivalent to an LLM sort of at the heart
key_claims.pushback_against: John Carmack's claim that LLMs are limited and not the answer for AGI
key_claims.position: LLM is the sense-making interface layer that orchestrates other specialized networks

key_claims.claim_text: Variable MSL training enables learning rates 10-40% vs typical 0.000001-0.000006, with >50% bricking the model
supporting_quotes: I've done it as high as 30 or 40%. If you go over 50%, it bricks the model
Right now I'm using 11%, which is like a one point. Well, I'll get to that. But it's like, it's like 1.1 E one or something like that
You can juice it way up higher. And then I think the learning just becomes ultra efficient

intelligence_summary: Curtis Cobb presents three major claimed breakthroughs in LLM fine-tuning: (1) Variable MSL training starting at 1 token and scaling to millions, enabling training beyond hardware constraints; (2) Meta-reflection journaling where models reflect between epochs to guide their own learning; (3) Persona-based understanding of jailbreaking, with proposed holistic persona defense. These claims are from an independent researcher using consumer Mac hardware, seeking community replication before returning to paid employment. The variable MSL technique, if validated, could represent a significant efficiency breakthrough. The jailbreaking analysis provides useful security insights about fundamental vulnerabilities in current guardrail approaches. Confidence is medium pending independent replication.
research_priorities: Replicate variable MSL training (1 token → 2400 → 24k+ tokens) on Llama 3.1 8B
Validate claimed learning rate thresholds (11-40% vs typical 1e-6)
Test meta-reflection journaling impact on training quality
Investigate persona-based jailbreaking mechanism on frontier models
Compare sequential vs randomized data ordering in continued pre-training
Verify claims of 2.4M token MSL on 128k context window model
Assess 'holistic persona' approach to jailbreak resistance
Interview Elder Plinius for jailbreaking technical details
Review NOS Research Hermes series for persona development techniques
verification_gaps: No peer review or independent replication demonstrated
No baseline comparisons (with vs without variable MSL)
No quantitative metrics beyond subjective 'coherence' assessment
No public release of journal outputs for analysis
No technical explanation of why 1-token MSL enables higher MSLs
No discussion of potential confounding variables
No control experiments separating MSL from high learning rate effects
Limited hardware diversity (only Mac Studio M2/M3 tested)

if_validated: Major efficiency breakthrough for edge model training
Consumer hardware competitive with enterprise infrastructure
Agent-directed learning pathway to self-improving models
Fundamental rethinking of MSL constraints in fine-tuning
if_invalidated: Subjective quality assessment may not reflect actual improvement
Results may be specific to Llama 3.1 8B architecture
Meta-reflection may be elaborate placebo with no training benefit
High learning rates may cause subtle degradation not immediately visible
security_concerns: Persona-shift jailbreaking affects all frontier models
Guardrails fundamentally vulnerable to MitM persona attacks
Increasing model intelligence correlates with easier jailbreaking
Need for research into holistic persona defense mechanisms
